title: Interleaved Region Failover Decision Tree and KV Patch Plan
creator: Avery Chen
description: Runbook and hotfix plan to manage interleaved cross-region outages that produce inconsistent KV state between leader and follower node groups. Focused on providing a deterministic decision tree for oncall, automated gating for traffic shifts across Hosted and Dedicated fleets, and a safe rolling KV resync hotpatch that minimizes customer-visible errors while respecting tenant isolation and SLAs.
background: We observed a pattern in recent incidents where partial network degradation combined with leader lease renewals caused KV shards to diverge. This caused tens of tenants to surface stale responses after regional traffic was shifted during an automated failover. Existing playbooks cover region evacuation and traffic draining but lack an explicit decision flow for determining when to (a) roll a KV resync hotpatch, (b) perform a surgical tenant rehome, or (c) perform a full region rollback. This ticket creates that decision tree, the code-level hotpatch steps, simulation checklist, and customer-facing comms templates.
acceptance_criteria: Decision tree documented and validated with SRE/runtime leads
Automated gating checks implemented in the traffic-shift service (canary + health checks)
KV resync hotpatch script (dry-run) tested in staging and can be applied with <10m downtime per shard
Oncall playbook pages created in runbook site with clear escalation paths and communication templates
Post-deploy synthetic test that asserts no more than 0.1% stale-kv reads for a sliding 30m window after rollouts
runbook_steps: Step 0 — Triage: Confirm scope (hosted, dedicated, or private). Identify affected regions, tenants, and whether leader leases were recently renewed.
Step 1 — Short-circuit traffic: If P95 latency > SLA or 5xx rate > 1% for >10 minutes, enable regional slow-path and reduce new tenant attach rates by 90%.
Step 2 — Snapshot KV state: Trigger immediate KV metadata snapshot for impacted shards and upload to secure bucket with timestamp and correlation ID.
Step 3 — Canary reroute: Shift 1% of traffic from impacted region to warm-standby region for 15 minutes. Verify success criteria (p95 latency, 5xx, cache-hit-rate) before proceeding.
Step 4 — Staleness probe: Run targeted consistency checks against critical tenant prefixes (user-facing flows) to measure stale-kv-delta and conflict rate.
Step 5A — If staleness < 0.05%: proceed with progressive traffic shift 1 -> 5 -> 20 -> 50 over 5m intervals, monitoring automated gating thresholds.
Step 5B — If staleness between 0.05% and 0.5%: schedule KV resync hotpatch on affected shards with 5m maintenance windows per shard and run post-resync verification before wider traffic shifts.

Step 5C — If staleness > 0.5% or conflict rate rising: abort automated shift, initiate tenant-level surgical rehome for high-priority customers and keep degraded region in read-only until full reconcile.

Step 6 — KV resync hotpatch (when triggered): 1) Pause leader lease renewals, 2) run deterministic merge utility with conflict-resolution policy (prefer last-write-known-good for non-critical keys), 3) write reconciled snapshot, 4) rotate read traffic back through reconciled shards.
Step 7 — Post-shift validation: Run full synthetic user journeys, run consistency probes for 1 hour, and confirm SLOs before closing the incident.
Step 8 — Customer comms: Use templated messages (see comms templates) and route escalations to Customer Success for P1 customers. Document mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.

Step 9 — Rollback heuristic: If after progressive shift error rate or stale-kv-delta increases by >2x from baseline, perform surgical rollback to prior region configuration and open a follow-up engineering hotfix ticket.
Step 10 — Close incident: Attach snapshots, timeline, and key metrics to the incident ticket; schedule RCA and follow-up actions within 72 hours.
monitoring_playbook: Primary metrics: p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, kv-cache-hit-rate, stale-kv-delta, shard-queue-depth, leader-lease-renewal-latency
Automated gates: canary_success_rate >= 99.5%, stale-kv-delta <= 0.05% for canary window, gpu-util < 85% on serving fleet
Dashboards: cross-region failover dashboard with tenant-level filters and a synthesized health score (green/yellow/red)
Alerting: Pager duty when canary_success_rate < 99% or stale-kv-delta > 0.2% for 10m
rollback_heuristics: Immediate rollback if 5xx rate increases by >1.5x and sustained for 10m post-shift
Rollback if >0.5% of customer-facing reads flagged as stale in 30m rolling window
Prefer surgical rollback (rehome or route back a tenant slice) over full region rollback when impact is localized
Document rollback step with exact DB snapshot id and traffic config in rollback ticket
communication_templates: Customer notify (initial): We are investigating degraded responses for services in REGION. We are actively shifting traffic and will provide an update within 30 minutes. Impacted tenants: TBD.
Customer update (post-canary): Canary traffic shows reduced error rate. We will proceed with a staged traffic migration with expected minimal interruption. Contact CS for priority requests.
Post-incident summary: Root cause, mitigation steps taken, customers impacted (list), mitigation timeline, permanent fix ETA
simulation_checklist: Create a staging cluster with synthetic cross-region latency injection
Run failure injection for leader lease renewals and verify KV resync tool preserves invariants
Execute progressive traffic shift simulation using traffic-replay tooling and validate automated gates
Dry-run customer comms with support rotation and timeline
hotpatch_details: Patch artifact: kv-reconcile v1.2.3 (container image sha: sha256:deadbeef...)
Safety: dry-run required for first execution, mandatory snapshot before write; admin approval required to flip dry-run flag
Expected time: 3-9 minutes per shard depending on shard size and conflict density
post_incident_actions: RCA within 72 hours with detailed timeline and action owners
Add staged rollback automation to traffic-shift service
Add targeted e2e tests to CI that simulate leader lease jitter
Review KV conflict-resolution policy with product and legal for high-sensitivity customers
Customer follow-ups: offer credits to P1 affected customers and schedule account-level postmortem calls
notes: This runbook explicitly balances operational speed with data correctness. The conflict-resolution policy used in the hotpatch defaults to last-write-known-good for non-critical keys and preserves tombstones; any deviation for regulated customers must be approved by Privacy & Compliance.
